# GraphicsService

- Inherits [`Instance`](instance.md)
- A **service**: get it with `game:GetService("GraphicsService")`
- **Not creatable**: it cannot be created with `Instance.new`

The graphics and display settings of this machine: the quality of the picture, the window and the frame rate. Use it to build an options menu.

The value of a setting is taken from the first of these that provides one: a command-line flag the game was started with, a value a script set in this session, the player's saved choice, the project's `project.toml`, the current quality level, and the engine's default. `GetSource` returns which one. A change takes effect at the next frame, and several changes in one frame are applied together.

These settings describe the machine, not the world. They are not saved with a scene, are not replicated, and do not affect the simulation. `SaveAsync` saves them for this player, and the game starts with the saved values. A dedicated server has no display: it reads the defaults, and setting a value there raises an error.

This page lists the members this class declares. Inherited members are
listed on the page of the class that declares them.

## Methods

### `ApplyPreset(level: Enum.GraphicsQuality)`

Sets every quality setting to the value that `level` gives it, replacing whatever a script, the player or the project set. `Auto` selects the level that was measured for this machine. `Custom` raises an error. The display settings, such as the window, `VSync` and the frame rate limits, are not part of a level and are not changed.

### `GetGroupLevel(group: Enum.GraphicsGroup): Enum.GraphicsLevel?`

Returns the level of a group of settings: the level whose values every setting in the group has. Returns nil if the settings do not all match one level.

### `GetMonitors(): { { Name: string, Size: Vector2, RefreshRate: number } }`

Returns the displays, in the order that `Monitor` indexes them.

### `GetRefreshRate(): number`

Returns the refresh rate of the display the window is on, in hertz, or 0 if it is unknown.

### `GetSource(setting: string): Enum.SettingSource`

Returns where the value of a setting comes from. `setting` is the name of a property, such as `"VSync"`. Raises an error for a name that is not a setting.

### `GetSupportedResolutions(): { Vector2 }`

Returns the fullscreen resolutions that the window's display supports, largest first. Returns an empty list where there is no display.

### `IsApplied(setting: string): boolean`

Returns whether a setting has an effect yet. A few settings are saved and reported before the renderer uses them; use this method to hide or disable them in a menu.

### `LoadAsync(): boolean`

This method yields: the calling thread waits until it completes.

Reloads the player's saved settings and discards what a script has set since. Use it for a menu's Revert button. Yields until it is done, at the end of the frame, and returns whether there was a file to read.

### `ResetToDefaults()`

Discards the values a script set and the values the player saved, so that the project's defaults apply. The player's saved file is not changed until `SaveAsync` is called.

### `SaveAsync(): boolean`

This method yields: the calling thread waits until it completes.

Saves the player's settings to `settings.json` in the player's own folder: the previously saved values, updated with what a script has set since. Yields until the file is written, at the end of the frame, and returns whether it was. After that, `GetSource` returns `Player` for those settings.

Returns false where there is nowhere to write: in a game that turned `[display] remember_player_settings` off, or in a run that has no folder of its own.

### `SetGroupLevel(group: Enum.GraphicsGroup, level: Enum.GraphicsLevel)`

Sets every setting in `group` to the value that `level` gives it.

## Events

Signals are deferred: a handler runs at the next resumption point, not
inside the call that fired the signal.

### `QualityChanged()`

Fires when the quality level or any quality setting changes, whatever changed it. It fires at most once per frame.
